grade.first_issue: The claimed n=2 guarantee is false. With Liu's marks at 1/5 and 2/5, Xiang may use just one mark at 7/10, splitting the length-3/5 interval into two pieces of length 3/10. The sorted pieces are 3/10,3/10,1/5,1/5, so Liu receives only 3/10+1/5=1/2<3/5. Thus Rule A applies.
grade.summary: The final formula (n+1)/(2n+1) is demonstrably wrong already for n=2; the actual value is 2^n/(2^(n+1)-1). The submission contains a correct lower-bound strategy for n=1 and correctly uses odd-ranked pieces to describe Liu's drafting payoff, but its n=2 construction fails and the general optimality claim is unsupported. Correcting the solution requires new lower- and upper-bound arguments.
strengths: Correctly recognizes that optimal alternating selection gives Liu the odd-ranked pieces by length.
The marking at 1/3 correctly shows that Liu can guarantee at least 2/3 when n=1.

errors.description: The n=2 lower-bound strategy fails against the admissible one-mark response at 7/10, which leaves Liu only 1/2.
The general assertion that every other distribution of Xiang's marks leaves Liu at least (n+1)/(2n+1) is neither proved nor true.
No universal upper-bound strategy for Xiang is supplied, even for the claimed general value; the n=1 discussion also establishes only Liu's lower bound, not maximality.
